statement_p1083.definition: Orders consume daily capacities on the closed interval [s,t] and stop at the first failed order.
statement_p1083.io: The input specifies n,m, capacities, and all order triples; output is 0 or two lines -1 and the first failed index.
statement_p1083.constraints: The restricted domain has positive capacities and demands, valid interval endpoints, n,m<=20.
statement_p1083.boundaries: n=m=1 and the interval [1,1] are legal; demand exceeding the sole capacity fails.
statement_p1083.samples: For capacity 1 and demand 2 on [1,1], the required output is -1 followed by 1.

statement_p17832.definition: The artifact defines entrance, hall, platform and transfer costs but omits an explicit bidirectional train rule.
statement_p17832.io: The header, per-line station/time pairs, queries and one output per query are specified.
statement_p17832.constraints: The restricted domain specifies distinct stations on each line, connected network, and distinct query endpoints.
statement_p17832.boundaries: The reverse query 2->1 on a single line is meaningful under conventional bidirectional metro service and mutual reachability.

statement_p5020.definition: Equivalence compares every nonnegative amount with unlimited positive-denomination coins, including new systems using other denominations.
statement_p5020.io: T groups each provide n and distinct denominations; each output is a minimum number of denominations.
statement_p5020.constraints: T,n,denominations have explicit positive finite bounds; denominations in each group are distinct.
statement_p5020.boundaries: Amount zero is represented by all-zero coefficients; standard notation Z_{>=0} is sufficient.
statement_p5020.samples: For [4,6,9], denomination4 is necessary, denomination6 cannot be made from4, and denomination9 cannot be made from even smaller denominations.

solution_p5020.algorithm: Sorted denominations use unbounded-knapsack reachability, keeping a denomination exactly when not already reachable.
solution_p5020.correctness: Discarded coins are generated by smaller kept coins; a kept coin is mandatory in any equivalent positive system by substituting representations of smaller coins.
solution_p5020.complexity: Sorting is O(n log n), updates at most O(nM), memory O(M), which fits the restricted bounds.
solution_p5020.implementation: The code parses all T groups, initializes reachable[0], uses increasing updates and prints one integer per group.

editorial_p5020.claims: The target is the exact minimum number of denominations in an equivalent system, not merely gcd agreement.
editorial_p5020.reasoning: Every deleted denomination is represented by kept ones, and kept ones come from the original system.
editorial_p5020.proof: A kept denomination c must occur in any equivalent system: otherwise substituting the representations of its smaller positive summands contradicts irreducibility.
editorial_p5020.complexity: Sorting O(n log n), at most n unbounded-knapsack updates over M amounts, space O(M), reinitialized for every group.

adjudication.rationale: Self-contained restricted closed-interval task; sample agrees with the definition.

finding.quote: if not any(coin % earlier == 0 for earlier in kept):
finding.observation: For [3,5,8], neither 3 nor 5 divides 8, so the code keeps 8 although 8=3+5. Both 3 and 5 are necessary, making the exact answer 2.

steps: Take one group n=3 with denominations 3,5,8.
Trace the divisibility tests: all three denominations are kept.
Remove 8 because 8=3+5;3 and 5 cannot be removed.

finding.repair_suggestion: Replace divisibility checks with reachability under unlimited kept coins.

coverage_overrides.algorithm: The code removes a denomination only if divisible by a single kept denomination; it misses sums of different smaller coins.
coverage_overrides.correctness: For [3,5,8],8=3+5, so the optimum is 2, but individual divisibility keeps all three.
coverage_overrides.complexity: At most n divisibility scans per denomination plus sorting; O(n^2+n log n), space O(n).
coverage_overrides.implementation: Input/output parsing is valid, but any(coin % earlier ==0) implements the insufficient deletion condition.
